title: Resolving the Kohayakawa--Kreuter Conjecture for Families
summary: A graph $G$ is $(a,b)$-sparse if every nonempty subgraph $H$ satisfies $e(H) \leq a v(H) - b$. We are interested in the conditions under which an $(a,b)$-sparse graph can be partitioned $E(G) = E(G_1) \cup E(G_2)$ such that for $i \in \{1,2\}$ we have that $G_i$ is $(a_i, b_i)$-sparse. Kuperwasser, Samotij, and Wigderson conjectured that a $(m,0)$-sparse graph can be partitioned into a $(1,1)$-sparse graph and a $(m,2m-1)$-sparse graph. We prove the conjecture in full.
